D021-D016_h001.question:
I’ve always been careful about my health—nursing taught me that. Since my husband passed five years ago, meals just haven’t mattered much. Lately, I make myself a little scrambled egg in the morning, maybe some broth at night. I’m down to 98 pounds, but my doctor keeps saying I’m too thin. I know I’m small, but I feel fine. It’s not that I *want* to be skinny—it’s just that when I think of eating something with fat, like butter or cream, my chest tightens. I fear it’ll go straight to my hips, *immediately*.  

I measure everything—calories, grams of fat. I read labels three times. If the package is unclear, I don’t eat it. Sometimes I rearrange the cans in my pantry by food group, just so they’re *right*. It helps quiet my mind. I don’t enjoy eating, not anymore. It feels risky. But I wouldn’t say I’m afraid of gaining weight in general—I just can’t stand the thought of losing control over what goes into my body.  

This has been going on for about nine months. I don’t see the point in increasing my portions. I tell myself I’m managing my health.
D021-D016_h001.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Bipolar II Disorder
D021-D016_h001.answer: C & B. Anorexia Nervosa & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D021-D016_h002.question:
I’ve been living alone since my wife passed five years ago, and lately, I just haven’t had much of an appetite. I skip breakfast most days—used to enjoy my eggs, but now it feels like too much. Lunch and dinner, I’ll have a little soup or toast, nothing heavy. The scale shows I’ve lost about eight pounds over the past three months, maybe more. I check it every morning—just a habit, really—but when I see it tick up even half a pound, I get… uneasy. Makes me tighten up a bit.  

I’ve started doing things with my food—arranging it just so on the plate, counting bites sometimes. If the toast isn’t evenly browned, I won’t eat it. I wash the same cup three times if I think there’s a spot. Doesn’t make sense, I know, but it feels necessary. It’s not that I *want* to be thin—I’m not chasing some ideal. I’m not looking in the mirror worrying how I look. It’s more like… if things aren’t right, something might go wrong.  

It’s just been harder to eat. Not that I fear gaining weight—I’m not a young man trying to look fit—but the numbers on the scale matter in a way I can’t explain. I don’t feel hungry, but I also can’t let myself just *let go*. I just don’t want anything out of order.
D021-D016_h002.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Bipolar II Disorder
D021-D016_h002.answer: C & B. Anorexia Nervosa & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D021-D016_h003.question:
I’ve always been mindful about eating healthy, especially since I work with kids and want to set a good example. Lately, though, I find myself cutting out more and more—no bread, no pasta, really limiting fats. It started with trying to feel more in control, but now even the idea of eating something high in calories makes me anxious. Like, if I eat a banana with peanut butter, I immediately worry I’ll gain weight overnight.  

I’ve lost about ten pounds over the past few months, not on purpose exactly, but stopping feels hard. I track everything, plan meals days ahead, and if something changes—like going out to dinner—I get really stressed. I rearrange my day around food. My husband notices. He says I’m rigid, that I won’t even try things I used to like.  

It’s not that I look in the mirror and hate what I see or think I’m overweight—that’s not it. And I don’t wash my hands fifty times or check the stove, so I don’t think this is OCD. But the rules I’ve made? If I break them, I feel like something bad will happen. I don’t know what—I just feel off. I keep asking myself: is this discipline… or is something else going on?
D021-D016_h003.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Bipolar II Disorder
D021-D016_h003.answer: C & B. Anorexia Nervosa & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D021-D016_h004.question:
I’ve been feeling really off lately. For the past few months, I just haven’t had much of an appetite—some days I skip breakfast and lunch without even noticing, and by dinner, I’m not hungry. I weigh myself every morning, sometimes more if I feel “off,” and if the number goes up even half a pound, it sticks with me all day. I keep thinking about what I ate, whether it was too much, and then I start rearranging things in the pantry—labeling, organizing. I do it automatically, like it’s the only way to quiet my mind for a bit.  

My husband says I’ve gotten too thin, but I’m just trying to be healthy. I don’t feel like I’m restricting, exactly—more like I’m trying to stay in control. The census work is part-time, so I’m home a lot, and I find myself stuck in routines—eating at the same time, using the same plate, measuring everything. But it’s not about looks. I just feel uneasy when things are unpredictable, especially food. I don’t know if it’s anxiety or habit or something else. I just know I can’t seem to stop.
D021-D016_h004.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Bipolar II Disorder
D021-D016_h004.answer: C & B. Anorexia Nervosa & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D021-D016_h005.question:
I’ve been keeping my meals very small—usually just tea in the morning, a plain salad at lunch, and maybe some broth in the evening. I know it’s not much, but I feel better, clearer, when I eat this way. Certain foods, especially anything fatty or sweet, make me anxious. It’s not just about weight—I don’t really think about that much—but the idea of eating a cookie or a piece of cheese feels… wrong. Like it will disrupt something internal, almost physically. I prepare my meals carefully, measuring and organizing everything, not because I’m counting calories exactly, but because it feels necessary to keep things in order.  

At work, restoring delicate paint layers, precision is everything, so maybe that’s bled into my routine. My husband says I’ve lost too much weight, and I can feel my clothes are looser, but I don’t feel unwell—just controlled. I do get irritable if my routine is interrupted, especially around food. Sometimes I weigh myself several times a day, not because I’m chasing a number, but because I need to check that things are still… aligned.  

It’s not about looking thin. It’s about avoiding the discomfort, the sense that something’s off if I eat differently.
D021-D016_h005.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Bipolar II Disorder
D021-D016_h005.answer: C & B. Anorexia Nervosa & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D021-D016_h006.question:
I’ve always been disciplined—had to be, with thirty years managing infrastructure projects. Lately, though, I’ve tightened things up more. I cut out bread, rice, anything starchy. Fats too—butter, oils, even salad dressing. I read the labels; I know what’s in the food. My wife says I’m too thin, but I feel better this way—lighter, in control. I’m down to 130 pounds now, which is lean for my height, but the doctor’s been after me to gain, and I just… don’t see the need. I feel fine. Tired sometimes, yeah, and my knees ache, but that’s aging, isn’t it?

The routine’s important. I weigh my food, measure portions, won’t eat unless it’s on schedule. If a meal’s unplanned, I get anxious. Not because of how I look—I don’t stare in the mirror or worry about that. It’s just that when things aren’t exact, my thoughts start racing, like something’ll go wrong if I slip. I’ve been like this for months—maybe a year. I know my wife worries. She says I’m obsessed. But I tell her: I’m just being careful. There’s too much uncertainty in the world to be careless with your body.
D021-D016_h006.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D021-D016_h006.answer: A & B. Anorexia Nervosa & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D021-D016_h007.question:
I’ve always been particular about order and control, especially at work—being a bank manager, things need to be precise. Lately, though, I’ve been focusing a lot on what I eat. I cut out carbs almost completely and avoid anything with fat. It started as just trying to eat “clean,” but now even the idea of eating those foods makes me uneasy. I’ve lost quite a bit of weight, and my wife keeps telling me I look too thin, but I don’t feel like it's a problem. Honestly, I feel better this way—sharper, more in control.

I weigh myself daily and stick to a very strict meal routine. If something gets thrown off, I get really anxious and need to repeat certain steps to make it feel right. It’s not really about how I look—I don’t spend time in the mirror or obsess over my reflection. But something just feels *off* if I don’t follow my rules around food. My doctor mentioned being concerned about my weight, but I’m not convinced it’s dangerous. I just know that changing my routine feels like losing control, and I can’t let that happen.
D021-D016_h007.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D021-D016_h007.answer: A & B. Anorexia Nervosa & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D021-D016_h008.question:
I’ve always cared about health, but over the past few months, I’ve really tightened up my eating. I plan every meal—strict counting, mostly under 800 calories a day. I feel better that way—more in control. My weight’s been going down, sure, and my husband noticed how pale I look. I get dizzy sometimes, especially in the afternoons between client meetings, and my hair’s been thinning, but I just chalk it up to stress. I’ve lost my period too, though it came back once or twice, so I don’t think it’s serious.  

Food takes up a lot of my headspace. I measure everything, wash the containers immediately, recheck labels even if I’ve used them a hundred times. If a meal doesn’t go exactly as planned, I feel this… tension, like something’s off for the whole day. I’m not sure why it matters so much, but it just *does*. I help couples build trust and balance, yet here I am, rigid about a salad. Maybe it’s just how I’m wired. I don’t feel fat—or afraid of gaining weight, exactly—just like if I stop managing it all, things might spiral. But is that so different from being disciplined?
D021-D016_h008.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D021-D016_h008.answer: A & B. Anorexia Nervosa & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D021-D016_h009.question:
I’ve been eating very little lately—maybe just a bite or two at mealtimes. Not because I’m not hungry, but... I don’t know, something just feels off about food. I pack my lunch like I always do, but I’ll sit in the bus during breaks and end up tossing it. Lost some weight, yeah, my clothes are looser, and my daughter keeps bringing it up. Says I look “too thin,” that I need to eat more. But I tell her I’m fine—probably just aging, metabolism slowing down. Doctors have asked too. I just say I’ve got a sensitive stomach these days.  

I’ve always liked things a certain way with food—cut everything just so, eat at the same time, never mix flavors. Lately, though, I can’t bring myself to eat unless the plate is... right. One crumb out of place and I lose the appetite. I wash my hands over and over before touching anything. I don’t *want* to do it, but if I don’t, it feels like something bad might happen.  

My wife used to say I was particular. Now that she’s gone, there’s no one to remind me to eat—or to stop. I don’t care much about how I look. Just feel like if I don’t follow the rules, things might get worse. But is it the food? My head? I can’t tell anymore.
D021-D016_h009.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D021-D016_h009.answer: A & B. Anorexia Nervosa & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D021-D016_h010.question:
I’ve just been trying to keep things under control, you know? With filming schedules all over the place—sometimes up at 4 a.m., other times not eating until wrap—I found it easier to skip meals than deal with the chaos. Breakfast? Honestly, I forget. Lunch gets pushed aside with all the notes and reshoots. Dinner’s usually just something light, if anything. I’ve dropped some weight over the past few months, sure, but I feel sharper, more focused. My ex-wife said she was worried, and my producer keeps offering snacks like I’m fragile or something. I told them I’m fine—better than fine, really.  

Food’s been… on my mind a lot. I count how many times I chew, whether the plate is symmetrical, if I eat in a certain order. It’s not about calories or wanting to be thin—I don’t even own a scale. It just feels like things have to be *right*, or the day spins out of control. If I break the pattern, I’ll redo the meal later, alone. Sounds excessive, I know. But it’s just how I cope. Doctors mention weight, suggest nutritionists, but they don’t get it—it’s not about the food in the way they think.
D021-D016_h010.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D021-D016_h010.answer: A & B. Anorexia Nervosa & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D021-D016_h011.question:
I’ve always been disciplined—part of surviving in fund management, honestly. Lately, though, my focus on food has taken over. I cut out carbs and fats almost completely a few months ago—not because I *hate* eating them, but because I feel like I don’t deserve to if I haven’t “earned” it. I track every gram, mostly to stay in control. The scale keeps going down, and honestly, I don’t hate it. When I see a lower number, I feel… competent. Like I’m succeeding at something, even if work feels chaotic.

My wife says I’m too thin, that I avoid meals with her, but I just tell her I’m not hungry. I prepare food carefully—everything separated, weighed. If something touches something else, I won’t eat it. It’s not about germs or superstition—I just need it a certain way. I don’t know what’ll happen if I don’t follow the rules. I can’t risk it. 

I don’t feel fat, not exactly, but if my body changes, will I still feel like *me*? I don’t feel anxious about getting heavier—I just know that this routine keeps everything… intact. I can’t slip.
D021-D016_h011.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Bulimia Nervosa
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
D021-D016_h011.answer: B & A. Anorexia Nervosa & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D021-D016_h012.question:
I’ve been trying to eat “cleaner” for the past few months—nothing processed, no sugar, mostly just salads, veggies, and plain chicken. I track every calorie; it helps me feel in control, especially with how chaotic work gets. I’m interning in PR, so there are all these events with food everywhere, people constantly grabbing bites, and I just… can’t. Even when I’m hungry, which isn’t often anymore, I can’t bring myself to eat much. I’ve lost weight—my clothes are baggy now—but I still see myself as heavier when I look in the mirror. My thighs and stomach look huge, even if others say I’m thin.

I wash my hands before handling food, every single time. I line up my utensils just right, and if something touches another item on my plate, I’ll remake the whole thing. It’s not about gaining weight—I don’t really think about that. It’s more about it feeling *wrong* if I don’t. Or if I do eat something “off-plan,” I feel so guilty, like I’ve ruined everything. I don’t know if it’s anxiety or discipline or what. I just know I can’t stop.
D021-D016_h012.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Bulimia Nervosa
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
D021-D016_h012.answer: B & A. Anorexia Nervosa & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D021-D016_h013.question:
I’ve always been a bit particular about food, but lately it’s taken up more space in my head. As a supervisor, I run a tight line—I expect discipline from my crew, and honestly, from myself too. Over the past few months, I’ve gotten strict with my eating—sticking to around 800 calories most days. I prepare the same thing: plain chicken, steamed vegetables, no oil. Nothing after 7 p.m.  

I’ve lost about 15 pounds since the beginning of the year, and my wife keeps saying I look too thin, but when I look in the mirror, my gut still looks soft, my face puffy. Doesn’t make sense, but that’s how it feels.  

The thing is, I don’t know if it’s about getting thinner or just… needing things a certain way. If the food isn’t cooked exactly, or if it touches on the plate, I can’t eat it. I’ll just skip the meal. It's not that I’m afraid of gaining weight—it’s more like something in me *resists* doing it differently. It’s not about fear, but I can’t seem to stop.  

My wife thinks I’m punishing myself. I just feel like if I let up, everything gets messy.
D021-D016_h013.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Bulimia Nervosa
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
D021-D016_h013.answer: B & A. Anorexia Nervosa & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D021-D016_h014.question:
I’ve been keeping to a pretty strict routine lately—meals included. I skip breakfast most days, not because I’m not hungry, but because timing matters. I work long hours at the office running diagnostics, and eating just throws off my focus. Even lunch gets delayed a lot—sometimes I don’t eat until late afternoon, other times not at all.  

I’ve dropped some weight over the past few months, but that wasn’t the goal. Honestly, I don’t even know how much I weigh. People keep commenting, saying I look thin, but when I look in the mirror, I see everything that’s still too heavy—my stomach, my face. I know it doesn’t make sense, but it feels real in the moment.  

The weird part is how food has started taking up space in my mind. I find myself arranging meals in specific ways, eating in a certain order. It’s not about calories—I’m not counting those. But if I break the pattern, it lingers. I have to do it again. I don’t like how it feels, but I can’t stop. It’s more about control than hunger, I guess.  

I just want things to feel precise. My car, my models, my day—they all need balance. This feels like part of that.
D021-D016_h014.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Bulimia Nervosa
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
D021-D016_h014.answer: B & A. Anorexia Nervosa & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D021-D016_h015.question:
I’ve been skipping meals pretty consistently for the past few months—breakfast is usually too early, and by lunch, I’m buried in code, so I just forget or convince myself I’m not hungry. Honestly, I end up eating one or two small meals by evening, nothing substantial. I’ve lost about fifteen pounds since then, but I don’t mind. In fact, when I weigh less, I feel… sharper. More in control. Like I’m doing something right, like it means I’m disciplined or capable.  

Food has become really structured for me. I have rules—specific ways of preparing things, exact portion sizes, certain foods I won’t mix. If something breaks the pattern, I get really uneasy and sometimes restart my day, even if that means not eating again. It’s not really about getting thinner, but more about things feeling *right*. I can’t explain why the rules matter so much—they just do.  

I don’t look in the mirror and see someone overweight or anything, but I guess I link my weight to how I judge myself overall. Still, I don’t think I’m obsessed with appearance. It’s more about order. Or maybe I'm just trying to stay ahead of something I can’t name. I just know that if I let the patterns slip, everything feels off.
D021-D016_h015.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Bulimia Nervosa
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
D021-D016_h015.answer: B & A. Anorexia Nervosa & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D021-D016_h016.question:
I’ve always prided myself on control—needed it in nursing, especially running a unit. Lately, though, food’s become… complicated. I don’t eat carbs anymore. Not even fruit or bread. Fats, either—no butter, no oils. I tell myself it’s about health, but honestly, if I eat something “heavy,” I feel like I’ll gain weight overnight. It’s not rational, I know. I’m not heavy—actually, I’ve lost about 12 pounds this year, down to 118 at 5’6”, but I can’t seem to stop. My ex keeps saying I look tired, but I can’t relax the rules.  

Meal prep takes hours. I wash the same container three times. I line up ingredients in a certain order—don’t ask why. If something touches another food, I redo it. It’s not about germs. It’s like, if I don’t do it right, something bad will happen.  

I don’t know if it's obsession or just discipline. I’ve always been detail-oriented, but now it’s… more. I don’t feel *fat*, really. But certain foods feel dangerous. I can’t explain why, only that I have to follow the routine. I’ve been like this for nearly eight months—started after a stressful shift—but it hasn’t gotten worse. Not exactly. Just… stuck.
D021-D016_h016.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D021-D016_h016.answer: D & C. Anorexia Nervosa & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D021-D016_h017.question:
I’ve been really careful with what I eat for about six months now. I used to record voiceovers from home and snack while working, but lately I just… can’t. Even the idea of having a full meal makes me anxious. I’ll take a bite or two—mostly plain rice or steamed vegetables—and that’s it for the meal. I tell myself I’m fine, but part of me keeps thinking if I eat anything richer, like pasta or anything with oil, I’ll gain weight overnight. It feels irrational, but the worry sticks.  

I’m 27, and I don’t have a scale, but I know I’ve lost some weight. Friends have mentioned I look thin, but I just want to feel “lighter,” like I’m in control. I’m not trying to be underweight, but adding more food back in feels wrong somehow.  

I also find myself stuck in loops—like if I eat something, I replay it in my head, wondering if I broke some unspoken rule. I don’t do rituals like counting or washing, but the thoughts? They don’t leave. They’re just there, humming in the background during sessions, affecting my focus. I cancel jobs sometimes because I’m too caught up in it. It’s not just about my body, though. It’s like the food itself has power now. I can’t trust it.
D021-D016_h017.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D021-D016_h017.answer: D & C. Anorexia Nervosa & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D021-D016_h018.question:
I’ve been keeping my meals really small—usually just black coffee and a rice cake, maybe some broccoli if I feel like I’ve slipped. I track every calorie; anything over 500 in a day feels like too much. I’ve lost weight steadily for the past few months, and honestly, I keep doing it because stopping feels like losing control. The scale going up even once gives me this panic I can’t explain.  

At work, I moderate violent content all day—gory stuff, really intense. After a while, I started needing to *do things* to feel clean. Like, I’ll eat one pea at a time, in pairs, or I won’t let food touch on the plate. If I break the pattern, I get anxious and sometimes just skip eating altogether. It’s not really about being thin—it’s more like, if I don’t follow the rules, something bad will happen, or I’ll feel contaminated.  

I don’t know if it’s about weight or if it’s just the rules I’ve made up. I can’t tell what’s me and what’s the job bleeding into my head. I just know that food feels dangerous, but I can’t say exactly why.

A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D021-D016_h018.answer: D & C. Anorexia Nervosa & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D021-D016_h019.question:
I’ve always been careful about what I eat, but lately it’s become… more structured, I guess. I work long hours at the museum cataloging artifacts, and to be honest, meals get in the way. Breakfast? I skip it most days—just don’t feel like I need it. If I’m not hungry, why force it? Same with lunch, sometimes dinner. I’ve lost a few pounds over the past few months, and people have noticed, but I’m not underweight—my doctor said I’m “within range,” though I know I could stand to lose a little more. I just… don’t like the idea of gaining weight. It makes me uneasy.

There are rules I follow with food—how I prepare it, when, how much. I wash the knives three times before chopping vegetables. I measure everything. If I don’t, I feel like something’s off, like the day will unravel. It’s not exactly about calories or fat—more about control, precision. Like if the food isn’t just right, I can’t eat it. I throw it away. I don’t enjoy eating much anymore, but it’s not because I’m afraid of getting fat. Or… well, I don’t know exactly why. It just has to be *correct*.

A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D021-D016_h019.answer: D & C. Anorexia Nervosa & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D021-D016_h020.question: I’ve always been particular about my meals—working in the hospital for forty years, you learn how important it is to keep things clean and proper. Lately, I prepare my food the same way every time, down to the teaspoon of olive oil. I eat very small portions—just a bite or two at lunch and a few crackers at dinner—not because I’m not hungry, but because, well, it just feels wrong to eat more. I’ve lost a bit of weight since my husband passed, and folks keep telling me I should eat, but I can’t seem to bring myself to do it. I don’t *fear* getting heavier exactly, but the thought of my clothes fitting tighter… it unsettles me. Still, I wouldn’t say I’m focused on my figure. It’s more that something *feels off* if I don’t follow my routine with the food—the arranging, the timing, the way it’s cut. I know it sounds silly, but skipping a step gives me this tightness in my chest. I don’t know if it’s obsession or caution. I just know I can’t change it. This has been going on for months—longer, really, but it’s gotten harder to keep up.

A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D021-D016_h020.answer: D & C. Anorexia Nervosa & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D021-D016_h021.question:
I’ve been skipping meals lately—especially breakfast and lunch—because I just don’t feel like eating when I’m heads-down coding. Sometimes dinner gets pushed off too. I know I’m a bit underweight, but I feel fine, honestly. My coworkers have mentioned it, and my sister keeps texting me about “eating something real,” but I don’t see the big deal.  

I avoid certain foods, like anything really rich or fried. Not because I hate them, but I get this thought in my head that if I eat a burger or pizza, I’ll immediately gain weight, like overnight. It’s not like I’m terrified of food, but I feel better controlling what goes in.  

There’s also this thing where I have to organize my groceries in a certain way—like, protein on the left, veggies on the right, everything in order. And sometimes I count calories in my head, not because I want to, but because it sticks. It’s like a loop. I don’t love doing it, but stopping feels wrong.  

I wouldn’t say I’m obsessed with my weight. I don’t check mirrors all the time or anything. But the food rules? They’re just easier to follow than break. I’ve been like this for a few months—enough that people notice, but not enough that I think I need to change.
